title: Clarify rerank endpoint ergonomics: top_k behavior, input schema, structured output, and pagination
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: This ticket standardizes the Rerank API ergonomics to reduce confusion for users and improve compatibility across SDKs. Goals: 1) Define unambiguous top_k semantics (ties, stable ordering, and score thresholds). 2) Propose a compact, forward-compatible input schema that supports per-item metadata and optional embeddings. 3) Design structured output that separates ranking metadata (scores, normalized scores, provenance) from content payloads. 4) Add cursor-based pagination for large candidate pools and document clear consistency guarantees. Rationale: Customers building reranking layers repeatedly ask about: how top_k interacts with negative values, whether the input list is mutated, how to page results deterministically, and how to attach per-candidate metadata that survives reranking. Closing these gaps will reduce SDK complexity, improve latency for large candidate sets (by enabling streaming + early cutoff), and make downstream metrics and audits easier.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API spec updated in repo (openapi.yaml) with new request/response examples. 2) SDKs (python/js) implement consistent top_k semantics and pagination helpers. 3) Regression tests verifying ordering stability and pagination consistency across models. 4) Performance benchmark demonstrates <=5% median latency increase for small pools (<=50) and >40% latency improvement for large paged flows when using cursor-based fetch + early cutoff. 5) Migration guide published in docs with examples for common client patterns.
migration_plan: 1) Publish spec and migration guide (docs/redwood/rerank-v2.md). 2) Release SDK helpers that wrap new fields and provide backward-compatible shims for top_k and pagination. 3) Pilot with two internal customers (search and recommendations teams) on beta default. 4) Gradual rollout: API supports both legacy and v2 flags for 4 weeks, then deprecate legacy after feedback. 5) Communicate breaking changes and provide automated conversion scripts for common patterns.
performance_targets:
- Small pools (<=50): maintain median latency within +5% of current baseline when using new structured output.
- Large pools (500-10k): enable cursor streaming and early cutoff to reduce 95th percentile latency by >=40% for typical queries.
- Memory: per-request peak additional memory usage should be <10% on our runtime for v2 flow.
- RPS: no regression in throughput for dedicated nodes with batching enabled.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: schema validation, top_k edge cases (k=0, k>n, negative k rejected), stable ordering for equal scores.
Integration tests: end-to-end rerank with embeddings vs direct model scoring.
Performance tests: synthetic candidate pools (10, 100, 1000, 10k) across models and quantization profiles.
Canary: enable for 5% of hosted traffic with per-route opt-in and observability dashboards for latency, cost per embed/token, and result stability.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Design sign-off + spec merge. Phase 2: SDK feature PRs and tests. Phase 3: Internal pilot with search and recommendations. Phase 4: Canary on hosted API (5% traffic) for 2 weeks. Phase 5: Gradual rollout to 25%/50%/100% with rollback hooks.
Rollback criteria: >5% regression in mean latency for small pools OR >2% increase in incorrect top-1 for monitored query set.
